Common.Loading: Reading compendiums… (only slow the first time)

Plan.SheetHint: Sheet plan — picks up from the sheet as it is now and plans the levels ahead. You can apply it when you level up.
Plan.FreeHint: A build from scratch — apply it to an existing character with 'Rebuild with this'.
Plan.DeleteBody: Delete the plan '{name}'? This cannot be undone.
Plan.FreeNote: A build from scratch. Applying it rebuilds the character with this build (up to the current level). Gear, coins and effects are kept.
Plan.ConvertHint: Keeps the sheet as it is for the levels so far, and turns this into a plan that carries over only the picks for later levels.
Plan.RebuildBody: {actor} will be rebuilt with this build up to level {level}.
Plan.RebuildLoseList: {abc} · {feats} feats · {spells} spells · attribute boosts · skill ranks
Plan.RebuildKeep: Gear, coins, effects, conditions and HP are kept. This can't be undone — duplicate the actor first if you want a backup.
Plan.RebuildDone: {name} — rebuilt with the new build ({n} changes). This plan now follows the sheet.
Plan.ConvertAsk: Continue '{name}' from the current sheet? The levels so far will match the sheet; the feats, skills and spells picked for later levels are kept.

Top.PreviewHint: Preview attributes, skills and statistics at this level

List.PickHint: Click an entry on the left to see it here. Double-click or press 'Choose' to pick it.
List.LegendHint: Prerequisites are read from their text. ? means a prerequisite the builder can't judge automatically (worships a deity, can cast focus spells, 'A or B' …) — read it yourself. ? entries stay visible even with 'Prerequisites met only' on.
List.LegacyDisabled: The GM has hidden legacy content for the whole world in the settings.
List.BoostHint: Only options that boost every attribute you picked (fixed boosts or a choice of two — free boosts don't count)

Pick.HeritageHint: This ancestry's heritages first, then versatile heritages (any ancestry).
Pick.ArchetypeHint: Archetype feats: take the Dedication feat first, then that archetype's feats. Another Dedication feat only after two more feats from that archetype.
Pick.DeityHint: Not required. Classes that need a deity (cleric, champion …) choose one here. Click it again to deselect.

Locked.Sheet: Up to level {level} this plan follows the sheet; it plans from the next level onward.
Locked.FreeHint: To try a different ancestry, background or class, add an 'A different build from scratch' plan with + above.
Locked.UnlockHint: Allow changing the feats, attribute boosts and skill increases of levels already on the sheet.
Locked.RelockHint: Lock again (your changes stay in the plan).
Locked.UnlockBody: Levels up to Lv {level} are already on the sheet. Once unlocked, you can change their feats, attribute boosts and skill increases in the plan, and applying the plan then replaces the sheet's feat in that slot (the original feat is deleted). Ancestry, background and class stay locked.

Attr.Title: Attribute boosts
Attr.Hint: Choose the boosts from your ancestry, background and class, plus 4 free boosts at level 1. Levels 5, 10, 15 and 20 give 4 more each. From level 5, boosting an attribute that's already +4 or higher is a partial boost (two make +1).
Attr.AltToggle: Alternate ancestry boosts: 2 free boosts instead of the fixed boosts and flaw
Attr.HintGradual: Choose the boosts from your ancestry, background and class, plus 4 free boosts at level 1. Gradual Ability Boosts is on: instead of 4 boosts at levels 5, 10, 15 and 20, you get one at each of levels 2–5, 7–10, 12–15 and 17–20 (a different attribute each time within those four) — pick them on each level's page; the numbers below show which level boosted what. At +4 or higher a boost is partial (two make +1).
Attr.Key2Hint: The second class's key attribute boost and class DC (Dual Class Items). A class boost that would raise an attribute already at +4 is dropped.

Skills.Title: Skills (level 1)
Skills.Hint: Skills from your class and background are trained automatically. Additional skills to pick: {n} ({left} left), including your Intelligence modifier.
Skills.Auto: Trained by your class or background

Level.IncreaseHint: At this level a skill can be raised up to {rank} (master from level 7, legendary from level 15).
Level.BoostHint: Four different attributes. At +4 or higher a boost is partial (½); the second partial boost gives +1.
Level.Nothing: Nothing to choose at this level.
Level.RaiseApply: Raise to level {level} and apply the plan
Level.DetailHint: Click a feat or feature to read it here.
Level.BoostTakenAt: Already boosted at level {level} (same group of four levels)
Level.BoostGradualHint: Gradual Ability Boosts: one boost at each of levels {from}–{to}, a different attribute each time. At +4 or higher a boost is partial (½); the second partial boost gives +1.

Overview.UploadHint: Upload a picture (large images are shrunk automatically)
Overview.TokenHint: Token image (the portrait is used if none)
Overview.Ring: Use a token ring (portrait inside the ring)
Overview.AllSet: Everything up to level {level} is chosen.
Overview.CreateHint: Creates a level {level} character. The rest of the level plan stays on the sheet, ready to apply when you level up.
Overview.CreateNeed: Choose ancestry, heritage, background, class, key attribute, the 4 level-1 boosts and level-1 skills first.
Overview.ApplyCurrent: Apply what's missing up to level {level}
Overview.StatsNeed: Choose an ancestry and a class to see numbers.

Detail.ChoiceAsk: PF2e will ask {n} more choice(s) when applying to the sheet.
Detail.ToChatHint: Post this to chat as a card so the GM can see what you picked.

Stat.Note: Calculated by PF2e. Equipment, choices made when applying, and items granted by feats may be missing.

Compare.Title: Compare — {name}
Compare.Note: Green: better than the first column; red: worse. Previews are approximations (no equipment or later choices).

Create.Confirm: Create {name} as a level {level} character? PF2e may ask a few questions afterwards.
Create.NoGM: A GM must be online to create a character (the GM's client creates it).
Create.Timeout: No response from the GM. Try again in a moment.
Create.NoUpload: You may not upload files. Ask the GM for the 'Upload New Files' permission.

Apply.Title: Apply the plan up to level {level}
Apply.Body: The following will be added to the sheet (nothing already there is replaced):
Apply.Prompts: PF2e asks for any choice the plan left open.
Apply.Nothing: Nothing to apply — the sheet already follows the plan.

Card.Title: {name} — level {level}!
Card.Body: What builder plan '{plan}' has set up to this level:

Welcome.Title: Character Builder
Welcome.Body: You don't have a character yet. Build one step by step? (You can always open it with 'Create Character' in the Actors tab.)

Translation.Title: Korean translation
Translation.Body: The character builder is tuned to the Rutz Korean translation module (names, descriptions, prerequisites). Using it alongside is recommended.
Translation.Hint: This notice is shown only once. The builder also works with other translations.

Settings.PerPlayerHint: How many characters a player may create with the builder (0 = no limit). Characters already assigned count too. GMs have no limit.
Settings.Ownership: Other players' access to new characters
Settings.OwnershipHint: 'Follow the world' uses the default access most player characters in this world have. The creating player is always the owner.
Settings.AllowLevelUp: Players may raise their level in the builder
Settings.AllowLevelUpHint: When off, only the GM raises levels; players just apply their plan to the level they've reached.
Settings.LevelUpCardHint: When a character gains a level, its owner gets a whispered card with an 'Apply the plan' button.
Settings.PromptNew: Offer the builder to players without a character
Settings.PromptNewHint: On login, players without a character are asked whether to open the builder.
Settings.FolderHint: Actor folder name (blank: no folder). Created if missing.
Settings.PacksHint: Comma-separated pack IDs (e.g. pf2e.feats-srd, my-homebrew.feats). Blank: picked automatically by name (feat · ancestr · heritage · background · class).
Settings.TrModuleHint: Blank: looks for a Korean translation module with 'rutz' in its ID, title or authors.
Settings.TrUrlHint: Manifest or page URL shown in the notice (optional).
Settings.HideLegacyHint: Hides legacy entries in every user's builder in this world. Off by default (legacy included); when on, the per-window 'Include legacy' toggle is disabled. Existing plans are kept.
Settings.PacksMenuHint: Choose which packs ancestries, classes and feats are read from, and whether homebrew in the world's Items tab is read too. By default, companion modules' animal and eidolon packs (Companion Compendia, etc.), packs disabled in the compendium browser, and system packs replaced by a translation module are left out.
Settings.TidyChoicesHint: In the 'choose one' windows PF2e opens when adding a class or feat (bard muse, cleric doctrine …), leave out packs disabled in the compendium browser and system packs replaced by a translation, and list each option only once. Answers picked in the builder are applied without a window regardless of this setting.
Settings.LevelCantripsHint: For spellbook and familiar classes (wizard, witch …), a cantrip may count as one of the two spells learned each level. The rules text ('ranks for which you have spell slots') is ambiguous — decide at your table.
Settings.AutoClassSpellsHint: Even when a feat or class feature is gained outside the builder (directly on the sheet), the spells it grants (e.g. a witch lesson's hex and familiar spell) are added to the spellcasting entries automatically.
Settings.AllowRebuild: Players may rebuild their character in the builder
Settings.AllowRebuildHint: When off, only the GM can rebuild a character from a from-scratch build.
Settings.SlotClassBonus: Table rule: extra class spell slots
Settings.SlotClassBonusHint: Adds this many slots to every rank the class table has slots in (0 = as written). Used when the builder sets slots and in the planner's spells-per-day. The builder only raises slots, never lowers them, so numbers set by hand stay.
Settings.SlotArchetypeHint: Slots per rank the builder gives an archetype's spellcasting entry for each rank its basic/expert/master spellcasting feats have opened (as written: 1). “Don't touch” leaves archetype entries alone. The entry is found by name (one with the archetype's class in it, e.g. “Archetype Psychic”) and isn't created if missing. Raised only, never lowered.
Settings.SlotStrays: Warn about archetype spells in the class entry
Settings.SlotStraysHint: Names spells in the class's spellcasting entry that look like they came from an archetype's list (not on the class's tradition). Turn off if your table allows it.

Ask.Title: Choices
Ask.Body: {name} has choices. Answer now and PF2e won't ask again when applying.

Pending.Title: Not chosen yet
Pending.Asks: Choices PF2e will ask while applying: {n}
Pending.Hint: If you continue, empty slots are left empty (you can fill them on the sheet later).

Spells.Title: Spell plan
Spells.Hint: Choose how the character casts and pick the spells to learn each level (spellbook / repertoire). Creating the character or applying the plan sets up the spellcasting entry automatically, along with the spells granted by the class and subclass choices (muse, bloodline, doctrine …) — e.g. a bard's Counter Performance, Courageous Anthem and muse spells. Focus spells go into their own focus spell entry.
Spells.NoCastingHint: Pick a tradition if your class casts spells.
Spells.SubclassHint: This class's tradition depends on a subclass (bloodline, patron …) — pick it yourself.
Spells.AtLevel: Spells to learn at this level (up to rank {rank})
Spells.PickHint: You can pick several — double-click or 'Choose'; do it again to remove. Faded rows are spells already planned at another level.
Spells.ListHint: This class prepares from its tradition's entire list each day, so there's nothing to learn. You can still note spells you use often here.
Spells.NoClassSpells: No spells from class features, subclass or planned feats yet (they appear once you choose a patron, bloodline, muse, etc.).
Spells.ClassGives: Spells your class grants up to level {level} (depends on planned feats)
Spells.Mode_book: Spellbook: record a set number at 1st level, then add 2 spells of any rank each level. Each day, prepare as many as your slots allow.
Spells.Mode_rep: Repertoire: learn one spell of a rank each time you gain a slot of that rank (slots = spells known).
Spells.Mode_list: Whole list: each day, prepare as many as your slots allow from your tradition's entire list; there are no spells to learn.

Learn.WizardNote: Plus 2 1st-rank curriculum spells, and 1 curriculum spell for each new rank.
Learn.WitchNote: Plus 1 patron spell (known by your familiar), granted by your patron.
Learn.NecroNote: Harm is added to your spellbook separately.
Learn.ClericNote: Divine font gives extra heal/harm slots (4 at level 1, 5 at level 5, 6 at level 15).
Learn.SorcNote: The first spell of each rank (and one cantrip) comes from your bloodline and is not counted here.

Extra.Psychic: Your conscious mind grants 3 extra psi cantrips.
Extra.Animist: Apparition spell slots and apparition cantrips are separate.
Extra.Sorcerer: Bloodline spells are included in these slots.
Extra.Wizard: Plus one curriculum slot per rank.

Spells.ResyncHint: Adds the spells granted by the sheet's class features and feats (patron, lessons, bloodline …) to the spellcasting and focus entries, and sets the daily slots from the class table. Spells from an archetype's features (Psychic Dedication's conscious mind, etc.) are left out.
Spells.Strays: “{entry}” has spells that look like they came from an archetype's list: {list} — they aren't on this class's tradition. Remove them unless they were picked on purpose. Archetype spells belong in the archetype's own entry, with one slot per rank by the archetype rules.
Spells.Tick: Check to learn it at this level

DeityAlignment.Hint: Legacy alignment: {alignment} (the deity's own, not its followers' allowed alignments)

Packs.Title: Compendiums the builder reads
Packs.Hint: Only checked packs appear in the builder lists (ancestries, heritages, backgrounds, classes, deities, feats, spells). Rows changed from the default are highlighted.
Packs.Saved: Compendium selection saved. Open builders will reload.
Packs.WorldHint: Homebrew ancestries, heritages, backgrounds, classes, deities, feats and spells made right in the Items sidebar (not in a compendium). {n} here now.
Packs.World_visible: Players see only the ones they have permission for (Limited or better)

Choice.PickHint: Click an entry to read it on the right; double-click or press 'Choose' to pick it.
Choice.AskPeek: Pick one to read its description here.

Setup.Title: Spell setup
Setup.Book: Write {c} cantrips and {s} spells in your spellbook → prepare {pc} cantrips and {ps} spells each day.
Setup.Rep: Learn {c} cantrips and {s} spells for your repertoire (cast any of them, up to your slots).
Setup.List: Prepare {pc} cantrips and {ps} spells from your whole list each day.
Setup.NoTradition: tradition not set (comes from your subclass)
Setup.FeatHint: Focus spells come from class features, your subclass and planned feats; change the feats and this list changes too. Creating the character sets up the spellcasting entries, focus spells and slots automatically.

Fam.Title: Familiar Builder
Fam.CannotCreate: You don't have permission to create actors. Ask the GM to create a familiar actor with this character as its master.
Fam.CountHint: Familiar and master abilities per day, as PF2e calculates them from class features and feats (Familiar, Enhanced Familiar, witch's familiar …).
Fam.NoFamiliar: No familiar actor has this character as master. Create one above.
Fam.PickHint: Click an ability to read it and its prerequisites here. Double-click to add.
Fam.Patron: Granted by a witch's patron — applied automatically with the patron, not chosen separately.
Fam.Specific: Only for a specific familiar ({folder}) — have the GM confirm yours qualifies.

KindHint.master: Abilities you (the master) gain — they count with the familiar abilities.
KindHint.special: Abilities only certain familiars (object familiars, undead, shikigami …) or witch patrons have. Not available to just any familiar.

Need.Rank: Can cast rank {n} spells using spell slots
Need.Cantrips: Can prepare cantrips or add them to a repertoire

Ask.Shadow: Shadow familiar only (any familiar for a shadowcaster)

Homebrew.NoTable: If this class casts spells: the builder has no spell table for it (homebrew or from another module), so spells per day and how many to learn aren't counted. You can still pick a tradition above and add spells — or ask the GM to set it up.
Homebrew.NoTableGm: If this class casts spells: the builder has no spell table for it (homebrew or from another module). Set it up once and every character of this class in this world gets spells per day and spells to learn.
Homebrew.Title: Spellcasting — {name}
Homebrew.FormHint: How {name} casts. Start from a printed class that works the same way, then change what differs.
Homebrew.LikeHint: Fills in the fields below from that class.
Homebrew.Slots_full: 3 per rank (wizard, cleric, druid, bard, witch)
Homebrew.Learn_book: Spellbook — a start at level 1, then some each level
Homebrew.Learn_rep: Repertoire — one spell known per slot
Homebrew.Learn_list: Prepares from the whole list (nothing to learn)
Homebrew.BookHint: Cantrips · 1st-rank spells at level 1 · spells added each level after that (a wizard: 10 · 5 · 2).
Homebrew.WorldNote: Saved in this world for the class slug {slug}. Homebrew authors can ship this in the class item instead — see the wiki (flags.rutz-pf2e-builder.casting).

Dual.HintFirst: This world runs dual-class characters (Dual Class Items module): after the first class, pick the second in the next tab.
Dual.Hint: Dual class: both classes' features and class feats, a key attribute boost and a class DC from each, the better HP and proficiencies, and skill feats, general feats and skill increases at every level either class gives them. On the sheet, Dual Class Items keeps both class items and gives the second class its own feat ladder.
